title: Subtype prediction accuracy, both methods
caption: Accuracy on the 3,020 held-out TD-or-PIGD next visits shared by every model, with 95% intervals from resampling patients. The two methods' intervals overlap: no significant difference.

title: Confusion matrices
caption: Rows are the predicted class, columns the actual next label. Both methods under-call PIGD, which is the minority and clinically costlier class.

title: Per-class precision, recall and F1
caption: Both methods recover TD well and PIGD poorly: PIGD recall is about two thirds, so roughly a third of PIGD next visits are missed.

title: Cohort overview of held-out predictions per patient
caption: One row per patient, one column per visit position in that patient's own sequence. Held-out predictions only. Patients are ordered by follow-up length, not by accuracy.

title: Example patients, actual versus predicted over time
caption: Six patients selected by fixed rules on their observed label sequence. Predictions are offset vertically so they do not hide the observed label. Held-out predictions only.

title: Predicted versus actual clinical measurements
caption: The primary target of Method 2: nine held-out clinical measurements per visit. Correlation is high partly because the level is persistent; the baseline comparison in fig07 is the informative test.

title: Rich profile against its baselines
caption: Panel (b) is the key decomposition: the model clearly beats assume-no-change, but the rate and medication components each contribute only a small part of that gain.

title: Calibration of both methods
caption: Subtype probabilities from both methods track observed PIGD frequency closely. Rich-profile predictive intervals are slightly too narrow: coverage is below the nominal 0.95 in most domains.

title: Dimensionality and rate heterogeneity of the representation
caption: Panel (a) is the evidence that the representation preserves multidimensional variation a single subtype label discards.
